brief: The FOMC raised the fed funds rate 25bp to 3.75%-4.00%, the first hike since mid-2023, unanimously, citing inflation above the 2% target and declaring the Committee will deliver price stability. New Chair Warsh declined to submit his own dot-plot projections but reiterated the 2% commitment. The dot plot shows 12 of 18 participants expecting one more 25bp hike in 2026 (to 4.00%-4.25%), holding there through 2027 before small cuts in 2028-2029; the long-run median rose to 3.2% from 3.1%. Median GDP growth projections rose slightly to 2.3% (2026) and 2.4% (2027); unemployment is seen holding at 4.1%. PCE inflation is projected to ease but not reach 2% until 2029, with near-term inflation projections revised higher than June. PNC agrees with the median through 2026 but forecasts an additional hike in early 2027, taking its own path to 4.25%-4.50% versus the median's flat 4.00%-4.25%. Risks are balanced: sticky inflation could prompt faster hikes; weak growth from high gas prices could pause tightening even if inflation temporarily accelerates. Markets read the release as more hawkish than expected: stocks and gold fell, yields and the dollar rose, oil fell about 3% to just below $103.
